title: Taxation for a Dynamic and Fair 21st Century Economy
what_it_is: Taxation for a Dynamic and Fair 21st Century Economy

sections.label: Capital gains tax equivalence
sections.summary: A 20% capital gains tax on 5% returns equals a 1% wealth tax, and MOF draws about a quarter of revenue each from corporate, consumer and fee sources.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, for an asset that generates 5% returns, an entirely pedestrian capital gains tax of 20% is fully equivalent to a wealth tax of 1%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a typical year, MOF draws around a quarter of revenue from taxes on corporations, another quarter from those imposed on consumers, another quarter from fee and investment income and the rest from various other sources.

sections.label: GST impact on families
sections.summary: GST affects lower-middle- and middle-income families disproportionately more than the wealthy while contributing around 11% of revenue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Goods and Services Tax (GST), for instance, affects lower-middle- and middle-income families disproportionately more than the wealthy while only contributing around 11% of revenue.

sections.label: Global Minimum Tax effects
sections.summary: The OECD-led Global Minimum Tax agreement could weaken Singapore's attractiveness for headquarters and erode corporate sector incomes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The recently concluded OECD-led agreement for Global Minimum Tax could weaken our nation's attractiveness as a location for siting headquarter operations, which in turn could erode the incomes we currently receive from the corporate sector.

sections.label: Wealth taxes and regressivity
sections.summary: Wealth taxes help lower regressivity in the current revenue mix because they are progressive by design.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Wealth taxes also help fulfill additional objectives of lowering regressivity, as I mentioned, in our current revenue mix since they are progressive by design.

sections.label: Singapore Gini comparisons
sections.summary: Singapore's pre-tax Gini compares favourably to developed economies, but post-redistribution it rises to UK and US levels, falling to 0.375 during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Using comparable measures, Singapore's Gini, prior to taxes and transfers, actually compares favourably to many major developed economies, including those of famously egalitarian Scandinavian nations such as Denmark, Sweden and Norway.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, after taking redistribution into account, Singapore's inequality metric jumps to the top of the range, comparable to that of the United Kingdom and the United States.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, Singapore's post-tax Gini also fell significantly to 0.375 from 0.398 during the COVID-19 crisis, even as pre-tax Gini remains unchanged.

sections.label: Top 1% wealth share
sections.summary: The top 1% share of total wealth grew to around 34%, and those with $40 million or more rose 10% to over 3,700.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a consequence, the share of total wealth held by the top 1% grew to around 34% and the number of those with assets of $40 million or more rose by 10% to more than 3,700 ultra-high net worth individuals.

sections.label: Singapore cross-border wealth management hub
sections.summary: Singapore has emerged as a leading cross-border wealth management hub managing $1.2 trillion, just behind Switzerland and Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore has since indeed emerged as a leading cross-border wealth management hub managing $1.2 trillion in worth, just behind Switzerland and Hong Kong.

sections.label: Proposed net wealth tax
sections.summary: The proposal is a 0.5% tax on net wealth above $10 million, 1% above $50 million and 2% above $1 billion, designated to a special-purpose foundation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I have mentioned a number of possibilities, my simple proposal is to introduce a tax of 0.5% on net wealth in excess of $10 million, 1% above $50 million and 2% above $1 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This tax may be designated to a special-purpose foundation mandated to exhaust its entire endowment on an accrual basis over time with some flexibility in terms of the allocation of payouts toward Government-approved uses that are consistent with national priorities.

sections.label: Swiss cantons wealth and estate taxes
sections.summary: All but one Swiss canton maintain progressive estate taxes, and Zürich applies wealth taxes starting at CHF 77,000 for singles and CHF 154,000 for households.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Recent geopolitical developments in Hong Kong are a reminder that political stability and respect for property rights are far more important determinants for factors for siting one's immobile wealth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And all but on canton of Switzerland – the world's leading wealth centre – maintain progressive estate taxes, and the canton of Zürich – the beating heart of Swiss wealth management – applies wealth taxes even more aggressively, starting at CHF 77,000 for singles and CHF 154,000 for households, with the top bracket of a little more than CHF 3 million.

sections.label: Low taxes not a siting factor
sections.summary: A PWC report listing 12 factors making Singapore best in class for asset and wealth management included no low-tax factor.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, taxes feature so little in such decisions that in a recent PWC report that listed 12 factors that made Singapore "best in class within the region" for asset and wealth management, not one of these was "low taxes".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Wealth taxes can improve the diversity of our Government's revenue sources and help manage the societal dislocations that result from rising inequality.

sections.label: Singapore tax and transfer progressivity
sections.summary: Half of workers pay no Personal Income Tax, the top 10% of payers account for about 80% of revenue, and middle households receive about twice what they pay.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Almost half or 50% of our workers do not need to pay any Personal Income Tax.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Of those who pay, the top 10% of individuals account for about 80% of the total revenue.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Over 60% of the net GST from households and individuals is estimated to be collected from the top 20% of resident households, foreigners residing in Singapore and tourists.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And when we consider the entire system of taxes and transfers, for every dollar of tax a Singaporean household around the middle pays, they will receive around twice the amount in benefits.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Lower-income households receive even more – about $4 in benefits for every dollar paid.

sections.label: Singapore taxes as percentage of GDP
sections.summary: Singapore's taxes are 13% of GDP, lower than the OECD average of 34% and the Asia Pacific average of 21%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our taxes as a percentage of GDP are only 13%, much lower than the OECD average of 34% and the Asia Pacific average of 21%.

sections.label: Review of wealth tax
sections.summary: The Government will continue to review the wealth tax.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As mentioned, we will continue to review the wealth tax.

sections.label: GST assurance package and support
sections.summary: An assurance package of $6 billion is set aside for when GST has to be raised, alongside GST vouchers and social support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: What we have said is that as and when GST has to be raised, we have set aside an assurance package of $6 billion and this will be able to see through the middle-income for the GST increase for five years and the lower-income for the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We also have in place the GST voucher system as well as a comprehensive social support system that is targeted at meeting those most in meet.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have also said that as and when GST is increased, we will absorb the GST on publicly subsidised healthcare and education.

sections.label: Reallocating revenue to less well-off
sections.summary: The Government reallocates the revenue to support those who have less.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Government reallocates the revenue to support those who have less.
